definition: State–action–reward–state–action (SARSA) is an algorithm for learning a Markov decision process policy, used in the reinforcement learning area of machine learning.
details: It was proposed by Rummery and Niranjan in a technical note with the name "Modified Connectionist Q-Learning" (MCQ-L). The alternative name SARSA, proposed by Rich Sutton, was only mentioned as a footnote. This name reflects the fact that the main function for updating the Q-value depends on the current state of the agent "S1", the action the agent chooses "A1", the reward "R2" the agent gets for choosing this action, the state "S2" that the agent enters after taking that action, and finally the next action "A2" the agent chooses in its new state. The acronym for the quintuple (St, At, Rt+1, St+1, At+1) is SARSA. Some authors use a slightly different convention and write the quintuple (St, At, Rt, St+1, At+1), depending on which time step the reward is formally assigned. The rest of the article uses the former convention.

explainer.lead: SARSA learns a policy for a Markov decision process by updating values from the transitions an agent actually experiences. It matters because it learns on-policy, reflecting the behaviour the agent really follows.

tiers.eli5: You learn the value of a route by rating each step against the next step you actually take, not the best step you could have taken.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it when the learned policy must match the behaviour being evaluated, such as safe exploration. A pitfall is slow learning when exploration is noisy, since updates follow whatever actions were taken.
tiers.paperLevel: The Q-value update depends on the current state S1, chosen action A1, reward R2, next state S2, and next action A2. It was proposed by Rummery and Niranjan as Modified Connectionist Q-Learning; the name SARSA was suggested by Rich Sutton and appeared only as a footnote.

explainer.example: An agent in state S1 takes action A1, receives reward R2, lands in S2, and picks A2; the Q-value for (S1, A1) is updated using that full chain.
